WbHandled.description:
One mark as the RECIPIENT's board carries it: this node handled the message
with this id, at this instant. Written by `wb clear` alone. The
recipient is the board's own node, so it is not repeated here.

**A MARK WHOSE MESSAGE NO BOARD CARRIES YET IS KEPT**, because a clone can
hold the recipient's commit before the sender's. Nothing counts it and no
view renders it, and it joins its message when that arrives.

handled_at.description: When `wb clear` marked it, read from the clock at the write.

sender.description:
Who sent it, so a mark whose message has not arrived can still say whose
it is.

WbItem.description: One line of a node's board.

authored_at.description:
The stamp the board's markdown claimed, verbatim. **Untrusted, and
non-null only on a migrated row.**

node.description: The moniker of the node whose board this is.

recorded_at.description:
**The item's creation instant**, written by the service from the clock,
once, at the write. Not named `created_at`: see the note above this block.

seq.description:
Position within the node's items of that kind. Ties on `recorded_at` are
broken by insertion order, never by this value alone.

WbNode.description: A participant: the board's header block, modelled.

authored_at.description:
The stamp the board's markdown claimed, verbatim. **Untrusted, and
non-null only on a migrated row.**

heartbeat_at.description:
When this node last reported itself alive. Service-written; see the note
above this block for what a MIGRATED value means.

migrated_at.description:
When this node's board became the model's, written by the service.
**Absent on a node registered from its hand-authored header and not yet
migrated**, whose markdown on disk is still the board; every board write
refuses such a node.

moniker.description:
The two-letter moniker: the directory name, the routing key and the
handle, all one value.

recorded_at.description: Written by the service from the clock, once, at the write.

session_id.description:
Absent for a node that runs no session loop, which is how the human's
node is represented rather than by a special case.

WbSent.description:
One message as its SENDER's board carries it: every field only the sender
writes, and nothing the recipient does. The sender is the
board's own node, so it is not repeated here.

archived_at.description:
When the sender archived it, read from the clock at the write; its
presence is the archived state. Only a message its recipient has handled
can be archived, and an archived one leaves the recipient's inbox view
while `wb show --all` still lists it. Archived is a state, never a
deletion, as it is for an item.

**NOT A VALUE OF THE RECIPIENT'S `WbMessageState`**: that is derived from
the recipient's marks, and folding the sender's archive into it would give
one field two writers.

authored_at.description:
The stamp the entry's `## (...)` heading claimed, verbatim. **Untrusted,
and non-null only on a migrated row.**

edited_at.description:
When `wb edit message` last changed the body; its presence is the
`(edited)` mark, and it carries none of the old body.

fyi.description: Set when the sender expects no reply.

id.description:
**The message's id, the one key across clones.** Minted by the service
at the send, one per row, so each recipient of an announce has its own.
A mark names its message by this and nothing else: a minute anchor and
its `#<n>` are per-minute order, which a clone holding some of the
sender's messages, or holding them in another order, cannot share. A
message that predates this shape carries an id DERIVED from its old row
rather than minted ([`derived_message_ids`]), so every clone converting
the old shape gives it the same one. Ids sort in send order.

re.description: The timestamp of the entry this one answers, where it answers one.

recorded_at.description:
**The message's send instant**, written by the service from the clock,
once, at the write.

description:
One node's whiteboard: `whiteboard/<node>/board.json`.

**EVERY FIELD HAS ONE WRITER, AND IT IS THIS NODE.** Its items, the
messages it SENT, and its marks on the messages it has handled. A message
lives with its sender because the sender is the only node that writes it,
and the mark lives with the recipient for the same reason, so a node that
commits its own `board.json` and the inbox views it wrote has committed
everything its verbs changed.

handled.description: This node's marks on the messages it has handled, in id order.

items.description: This node's own items, in `seq` order.

sent.description: The messages this node SENT, in id order, which is send order.

title: Board
